title: Start VM 106 and bring the PalWorld service up on UDP 8211
commands: qm status 106 | grep -q running || qm start 106
qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-enabled palworld-server
qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-active palworld-server
verify: qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-enabled palworld-server
qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-active palworld-server
runbook:
## Prerequisites

- Proxmox VE host reachable as `root@pve` in a single shell
- VM 106 exists and is stopped (per ADD53, it was stopped for disk resize)
- QEMU guest agent installed inside VM 106 (per ADD65, `qm agent 106 ping` succeeded previously)

## Run this

```bash
qm status 106 | grep -q running || qm start 106
```

```bash
qm agent 106 ping
```

```bash
qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-enabled palworld-server
```

```bash
qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-active palworld-server
```

```bash
qm agent 106 exec -- ss -ulnp | grep 8211
```

## Verify

- `qm status 106` reports `status: running`
- `qm agent 106 ping` returns without error
- `qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-enabled palworld-server` returns `enabled`
- `qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl is-active palworld-server` returns `active`
- `qm agent 106 exec -- ss -ulnp | grep 8211` shows a listener on UDP 8211

## Rollback

- If `qm start 106` fails, run `qm config 106` to confirm the disk is attached (`scsi0: local-lvm:vm-106-disk-0,size=40G` per ADD53) and check `journalctl -u pvedaemon -n 50` for start errors.
- If `qm agent 106 ping` fails with "QEMU guest agent is not running", the guest agent is not installed or not running inside the VM. Install it inside the guest: `qm guest exec 106 -- apt-get install -y qemu-guest-agent` then `qm guest exec 106 -- systemctl enable --now qemu-guest-agent`. If the guest has no network, use the Proxmox console (`qm terminal 106`) to install it manually.
- If `systemctl is-enabled palworld-server` returns `disabled` or `masked`, enable it: `qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl enable palworld-server`.
- If `systemctl is-active palworld-server` returns `inactive` or `failed`, start it: `qm agent 106 exec -- systemctl start palworld-server`, then check `qm agent 106 exec -- journalctl -u palworld-server -n 50` for the failure reason.
- If no UDP 8211 listener appears, confirm the service is actually running and check its config for the correct port: `qm agent 106 exec -- journalctl -u palworld-server -n 50`.
